name: SN74HC165 8 Bit Parallel Load Shift Register DIP 16PIN

blocks.text: the SN74HC165 8-bit parallel-load shift register in the DIP-16 (PDIP) package.

blocks.v: 2 V to 6 V · Wide operating range
±4 mA at 5V · Can drive up to 10 LSTTL loads
SH/LD · Shift/Load (Active LOW). Loads parallel data when LOW; shifts when HIGH.
CLK · Clock Input. Shifts data on LOW-to-HIGH transition.
CLK INH · Clock Inhibit. When HIGH, clock is disabled.

blocks.text: Loading Data: Pull SH/LD (Pin 1) LOW to load the 8 parallel inputs (A–H) into the register. Data is loaded asynchronously (independent of the clock) .
Shifting Data: Pull SH/LD HIGH and CLK INH LOW, then pulse the CLK pin. Data shifts toward the serial output (QH) on each rising edge .
Cascading: Connect the QH output of one chip to the SER input of the next chip to chain multiple registers for 16, 24, or more inputs .
Unused Inputs: All unused inputs must be tied to VCC or GND to prevent floating CMOS inputs and erratic behavior .

blocks.text: Synchronous Operation: All flip-flops are clocked simultaneously, eliminating output counting spikes found in ripple counters .

Dual Clock Inputs: Separate clock pins for counting Up (CPU) and Down (CPD). The direction is determined by which clock is pulsed while the other is held HIGH . Important: Never leave both clocks LOW simultaneously.
Asynchronous Parallel Load (PL): Allows the counter to be preset to any 4-bit value by placing data on P0-P3 and pulsing PL LOW .
Asynchronous Master Reset (MR): Forces all outputs to LOW (0000) when pulsed HIGH, independent of clocks .
Cascading: Internal carry (TCU) and borrow (TCD) outputs allow multiple counters to be chained without external logic for multi-digit counting .
The operation is determined by the state of MR, PL, CPU, and CPD :
(H = HIGH, L = LOW, X = Don’t Care, ↑ = LOW-to-HIGH transition)

blocks.text: The UGE GP8212S module generates a standard 4–20 mA current loop from an I²C command. Use it to drive industrial inputs on PLCs, inverters, valves, sensors, and other 4–20 mA receivers.

blocks.text: The LM321 is a low-power, single-channel operational amplifier that serves as the single-channel version of the popular LM324 quad op-amp. blocks.text: Single-Supply Operation: The input common-mode range includes ground, so it can operate directly from a single supply without needing a negative rail or external biasing.
Low Power Consumption: With a quiescent current of only 430 µA (typical), it’s well-suited for battery-powered devices and portable electronics.

Stable with Capacitive Loads: The LM321 is designed to be stable with high capacitive loads, though you may need a small series isolation resistor (typically 50-100Ω) at the output if driving significant capacitance directly.
Internal Compensation: The device is internally frequency-compensated for unity-gain stability, simplifying circuit design.
Output Short-Circuit Protection: The output is protected against short circuits to ground (when V+ ≤ 15V), preventing damage from accidental shorts.
Input Voltage Range: The input voltage should not exceed the supply voltage. If an input is driven below -0.3V, excessive current can flow, potentially causing output phase inversion.

Variants: Different manufacturers may produce LM321 variants with slightly different specifications. For example, SG Micro’s LM321X offers a wider temperature range (-40°C to +125°C) and rail-to-rail output. Always check the specific datasheet for your exact part number.
Not Rail-to-Rail: The output cannot swing all the way to the positive supply rail; expect the high output voltage to be approximately 1.5V below V+

DC Bias Derating (Critical): X7R is a Class 2 dielectric. Capacitance decreases significantly when DC voltage is applied. A 10V rated capacitor may lose a substantial portion of its 4.7µF value at operating voltages near its rating . For critical applications, always check the manufacturer’s DC bias derating curve for this specific part. You may need to select a higher voltage rating (e.g., 16V or 25V) or a higher nominal capacitance value to ensure the required effective capacitance at your working voltage .

Capacitance Aging: X7R capacitors exhibit a gradual loss of capacitance over time, which is another characteristic of Class 2 dielectrics . This aging effect should be considered for long-life or precision applications.
Typical Applications: Commonly used as bulk decoupling capacitors on power rails, filters for DC-DC converters, and general-purpose bypass capacitors

blocks.text: The INA228 is a high-precision digital power monitor featuring a 20-bit delta-sigma ADC for accurate measurement of current and bus voltage. It supports both high-side and low-side DC current sensing and can measure bus voltages up to 85 V.

The module communicates with a microcontroller through I²C and can report current, bus voltage, power, energy, charge, and internal temperature. The STEMMA QT / Qwiic connectors provide a convenient plug-and-play interface for compatible development boards.

The INA228 measures the voltage across an external or onboard shunt resistor and calculates the corresponding current digitally.

For a module using the commonly supplied 15 mΩ shunt resistor, the module can be configured for different current ranges. For example, the Adafruit STEMMA QT/Qwiic implementation specifies up to approximately 10 A in its high-current configuration or 2.75 A in its higher-resolution configuration.

Important: The maximum safe current of a particular module depends on its shunt resistor, PCB copper, connector, thermal conditions, and operating environment. Do not treat the 85 V rating as an 85 V/10 A continuous power rating.
The module uses I²C for communication with the host microcontroller.

The actual maximum measurable current depends on the module’s shunt resistor and thermal design.

The INA228 itself operates from 2.7–5.5 V, while the monitored bus can be substantially higher, up to 85 V within the device’s specified conditions.

blocks.text: The PCF8575PWR from Texas Instruments is a 16-bit remote I/O expander that adds 16 general-purpose digital I/O lines to a microcontroller through a simple I²C/SMBus interface. It is designed for applications where additional GPIO pins are required without using more MCU pins.

The device operates from 2.5 V to 5.5 V, supports I²C communication up to 400 kHz, and provides an interrupt output for detecting changes on the input ports. Up to eight PCF8575 devices can share the same I²C bus using the three hardware address pins.
Up to 400 kHz I²C bus speed
TI currently lists PCF8575PWR as an active part number in the 24-pin TSSOP package.
The 16 GPIOs are organized into two 8-bit ports:

The PCF8575 uses a quasi-bidirectional I/O architecture, allowing each pin to function as either an input or output without a conventional direction-control register. After power-on, the I/O pins are HIGH.
Three hardware address pins provide 8 possible I²C addresses, allowing multiple PCF8575 devices to operate on the same I²C bus.
This makes it possible to expand a system by up to 128 additional I/O pins using eight devices, subject to bus loading and system design considerations.
The INT output is an open-drain interrupt signal that can notify the host MCU when an input state changes. This can reduce the need for continuously polling all 16 inputs.
Verify the pin numbering against the TI datasheet when creating the PCB footprint or assembly documentation.
Typical applications include 3.3 V and 5 V systems.
The device is controlled through the I²C interface.

blocks.text: The SN74AHCT125N from Texas Instruments is a quadruple non-inverting bus buffer featuring four independent logic channels with 3-state outputs. Each channel can pass a digital signal from its input to its output or disconnect its output by using the individual Output Enable (OE) control.

The AHCT logic family features TTL-compatible inputs, making the device particularly useful for interfacing lower-voltage logic signals with 5 V logic systems. The device operates from a 4.5 V to 5.5 V supply and is available in a through-hole 14-pin PDIP package.
Individual Output Enable (OE) for each channel
Suitable for digital signal buffering and logic-level interfacing
TI currently lists the SN74AHCT125N as an active device in a 14-pin PDIP package with a −40°C to +125°C operating-temperature range.
Each channel operates as a non-inverting buffer:
When OE is LOW, the output follows the input. When OE is HIGH, the output is placed into a high-impedance (Hi-Z) state, allowing multiple devices to share a common bus.
The device is controlled entirely through its digital inputs and Output Enable pins.
A bypass capacitor should be placed close to the VCC and GND pins in practical PCB designs.
Unused inputs should not be left floating; TI recommends tying unused inputs to VCC or GND.
1 × SN74AHCT125N Quad Non-Inverting Bus Buffer IC
The AHCT family uses TTL-compatible input thresholds, which makes it useful when interfacing logic signals to a 5 V system.
Unlike a simple 74HC125, the 74AHCT125 should be powered from approximately 5 V within its specified operating range.
The four channels are independently controlled through their respective OE inputs.
When OE is HIGH, the corresponding output becomes high impedance rather than producing a logic HIGH or LOW.

name: CH390H Ethernet Industrial-Grade Controller Chip QFN32
desc: CH390H Ethernet Industrial-Grade Controller Chip QFN32

blocks.text: The CH390H is an industrial-grade 10/100 Mbps Ethernet controller from WCH, integrating both an Ethernet MAC and PHY in a single IC. It provides an SPI host interface, allowing microcontrollers and embedded processors to add wired Ethernet connectivity with a compact external circuit.

The device supports 10BASE-T and 100BASE-TX, automatic negotiation, Auto-MDIX, IEEE 802.3x flow control, and includes 16 KB of internal SRAM. The CH390H is particularly suitable for embedded Ethernet applications where a compact, SPI-connected Ethernet controller is required.

The dedicated VDDIO supply allows the SPI interface to operate with 1.2 V, 1.8 V, 2.5 V, or 3.3 V logic, while the chip’s main supply is 3.3 V.
The CH390H is not a programmable microcontroller. It operates as an Ethernet peripheral controlled by an external MCU, MPU, or other host processor through SPI.
For example, Espressif provides a CH390H/D Ethernet driver for ESP-IDF.
The CH390H integrates both the Ethernet MAC and PHY, so a separate external Ethernet PHY is not required.
CH390H is an Ethernet controller/peripheral, not a standalone TCP/IP microcontroller. Network protocol handling is performed by the host system/software.
The chip provides a built-in unique Ethernet MAC address, eliminating the need for an external EEPROM solely for MAC-address storage.

desc: SN65DP159RGZ video interface IC chip QFN-48

blocks.text: The SN65DP159RGZ from Texas Instruments is a high-speed DisplayPort Dual-Mode (DP++) to HDMI retimer designed for digital video signal conditioning and conversion at the physical-layer interface.

It supports data rates up to 6 Gbps per lane, enabling 4K × 2K at 60 Hz video with HDMI 2.0-class electrical performance. The device integrates adaptive equalization, clock-data recovery, TMDS level translation, and programmable transmitter controls to compensate for signal loss and jitter in high-speed video interconnects.
Up to 6 Gbps per data lane
Programmable fixed equalization up to 16.5 dB
Supports Type-2 I²C-over-AUX to DDC bridge
TI lists the SN65DP159RGZR as an active 48-pin VQFN device with an industrial operating temperature range of −40°C to +85°C.
The SN65DP159 receives high-speed AC-coupled differential video signals and uses receiver equalization and CDR to compensate for losses and jitter introduced by PCB traces and cables.

At lower data rates below approximately 1 Gbps, the device can automatically operate as a redriver. At higher data rates it operates as a retimer, with the CDR restoring the timing of the incoming signal.
The programmable fixed equalization range extends up to 16.5 dB, allowing the device to compensate for different levels of channel loss.
The device provides HDMI 2.0b-compatible TMDS output and supports data rates up to 6 Gbps per lane, sufficient for applications such as 4K × 2K at 60 Hz with 8 bits per color.

The I²C interface allows control of parameters such as equalization, transmit settings, and operating modes.
The device is not a microcontroller or video processor. It performs high-speed physical-layer signal conditioning and retiming rather than video decoding, scaling, or image processing.

It supports up to 6 Gbps per TMDS channel, making it suitable for HDMI 2.0 applications including 4K × 2K at 60 Hz. The device integrates receiver equalization, clock-data recovery (CDR), retiming, and programmable configuration through I²C or pin straps.

The TMDS181 receives the high-speed HDMI/DVI TMDS signals, performs receiver equalization and clock-data recovery, and retransmits a cleaned-up signal. This helps compensate for random jitter, channel loss, and signal degradation caused by long PCB traces, cables, or other interconnects.

The device supports signaling rates up to 6 Gbps, enabling HDMI 2.0-class applications such as 4K × 2K at 60 Hz. At lower data rates below approximately 1 Gbps, the device can operate as a redriver; above this range it operates as a retimer.

blocks.text: The VL53L0X is a tiny 4.4 x 2.4 x 1.0mm module that uses VCSEL (Vertical Cavity Surface-Emitting Laser) technology to measure distance by timing how long it takes for a laser pulse to bounce back from a target . The GY-53 module adds a secondary microcontroller (likely an STM32) to allow multiple ways to read the distance data: by using I²C to talk directly to the VL53L0X, or through the easier-to-use UART and PWM outputs provided by the onboard MCU . A quartz crystal provides both series and parallel resonance. The series resonance is a few kilohertz lower than the parallel one. Crystals below 30 MHz are generally operated between series and parallel resonance, which means that the crystal appears as an inductive reactance in operation, this inductance forming a parallel resonant circuit with externally connected parallel capacitance. Any small additional capacitance in parallel with the crystal will thus pull the frequency downwards. Moreover, the effective inductive reactance of the crystal can be reduced by adding a capacitor in series with the crystal. This latter technique can provide a useful method of trimming the oscillatory frequency within a narrow range; in this case inserting a capacitor in series with the crystal will raise the frequency of oscillation. For a crystal to operate at its specified frequency, the electronic circuit has to be exactly that specified by the crystal manufacturer. Note that these points imply a subtlety concerning crystal oscillators in this frequency range: the crystal does not usually oscillate at precisely either of its resonant frequencies.

Crystals above 30 MHz (up to >200 MHz) are generally operated at series resonance where the impedance appears at its minimum and equal to the series resistance. For these crystals the series resistance is specified (<100 Ω) instead of the parallel capacitance. To reach higher frequencies, a crystal can be made to vibrate at one of its overtone modes, which occur near multiples of the fundamental resonant frequency. Only odd numbered overtones are used. Such a crystal is referred to as a 3rd, 5th, or even 7th overtone crystal. To accomplish this, the oscillator circuit usually includes additional LC circuits to select the desired overtone.

There are two ways to program the microcontroller: via USB using the built-in bootloader and via the serial 2-wire debug interface using a WCH-LinkE programming device.

On Linux you do not need to install a driver. However, by default Linux will not expose enough permission to upload your code with the USB bootloader. In order to fix this, open a terminal and run the following commands:
echo 'SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTR{idVendor}=="4348", ATTR{idProduct}=="55e0", MODE="666"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-ch55x.rules
echo 'SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTR{idVendor}=="1a86", ATTR{idProduct}=="55e0", MODE="666"' | sudo tee -a /etc/udev/rules.d/99-ch55x.rules

For Windows, you need the CH372 driver. Alternatively, you can also use the Zadig Tool to install the correct driver. Here, click “Options” -> “List All Devices” and select the USB module. Then install the libusb-win32 driver. To do this, the board must be connected and the microcontroller must be in bootloader mode.

The bootloader must be started manually for new uploads. To do this, the board must first be disconnected from the USB port and all voltage sources. Now press the BOOT button and keep it pressed while reconnecting the board to the USB port of your PC. The chip now starts in bootloader mode, the BOOT button can be released and new firmware can be uploaded via USB within the next couple of seconds.
WCH offers the free but closed-source software WCHISPTool to upload firmware with Windows via the USB bootloader.

You can also use chprog, a simple Python command line tool, to flash the microcontroller via the built-in USB bootloader. In order for this tool to work, Python3 with pip must be installed on your system. To do this, follow these instructions. Then install chprog via pip. To program the microcontroller via the serial debug interface, you will need a special programming device. The WCH-LinkE (pay attention to the “E” in the name) is a suitable option for this purpose and can be purchased commercially for around $4. This debugging tool is also compatible with other WCH RISC-V and ARM-based microcontrollers.
To use the WCH-Link on Linux, you need to grant access permissions beforehand by executing the following commands:
echo 'SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTR{idVendor}=="1a86", ATTR{idProduct}=="8010", MODE="666"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-WCH-LinkE.rules
echo 'SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTR{idVendor}=="1a86", ATTR{idProduct}=="8012", MODE="666"' | sudo tee -a /etc/udev/rules.d/99-WCH-LinkE.rules

blocks.text: The TNS-60kVA Three Phase Voltage Stabilizer is a heavy-duty servo motor controlled voltage regulation system designed for large industrial and commercial applications. It provides accurate voltage stabilization, ensuring reliable performance, equipment protection, and long operational life in environments with unstable power supply.
To ensure proper sizing and optimal performance, follow these recommendations:
For purely resistive loads such as heating elements and incandescent lighting, select a stabilizer rated at 1.5 to 2 times the total connected load.
For motors, pumps, air conditioners, compressors, and other inductive loads, select a stabilizer rated at at least 3 times the total load power.
For applications with high starting current (up to 5–8 times rated current), choose a stabilizer with capacity greater than 3 times the load power.

blocks.text: PH2.0 mm 5-Pin Crimped Cable — Typical Specs
Connector system: JST PH series (often called “PH2.0”) — common micro wire-to-wire / wire-to-board housing family.
Pin count: 5 pins (5 positions) standard PH housing.
Pitch: 2.0 mm (distance between center of adjacent pins).

Configuration: Double-ended cable (crimped terminals in both housings) — in your case usually female housings on both ends (reversed head / reversed polarity version is just reversed wiring colors or pin order).
Housing material: Insulating plastic (commonly nylon/PA based).
Crimp terminals: Tin-plated phosphor bronze or brass (typical for PH connectors).
Cable length: ~10 cm (visible in typical PH2.0 jumpers).
Wire gauge: typically ~26 AWG / 28 AWG stranded wire (common for PH2.0 assemblies).
Housing orientation: Straight inline on both ends (reversed head typically means the order of pins is flipped relative to wire colors).
Current rating: typically ~2 A AC/DC max per contact (dependent on wire gauge).
Contact resistance: initial ~ ≤10 mΩ–20 mΩ (varies by crimp and plating).
Dielectric withstanding voltage: ~ 800 V AC / 1 min typical test.
Mating cycles: PH series connectors are designed for repeated mating/unmating — typical mechanical endurance is in the low hundreds of cycles (exact value from manufacturer).
Use cases: Low-voltage DC signal & power connections for small devices, PCBs, sensors, modules, microcontrollers, battery harnesses, etc.

“Reversed head” usually refers to wiring or orientation reversal — meaning the pin order is flipped relative to a standard cable, not a different connector family. It’s still PH2.0 with the same shape and pitch, just wired in reverse order so Pin-1 on one end goes to Pin-5 on the other (or similar).
The physical housings and crimp terminals are identical in size/fit to standard PH2.0 crimp housings — only the wire order differs.
Plug-in wiring between PCBs and modules with JST-PH2.0 male headers.
Battery packs and small power modules (e.g., LiPo connectors on micro drones).
Signals, I2C/UART power + data harnesses, custom jumpers.
Robotics, LED drivers, sensor arrays where compact 2 mm pitch harnessing is needed.

name: WS2812B Programmable RGB LED Chip 3535 SMD Package
desc: WS2812B Programmable RGB LED Chip 3535 SMD Package

blocks.text: WS2812B Programmable RGB LED Chip 3535 SMD Package
Supply voltage (VDD): ≈ 5.0 V (typical operating range shown in datasheets around 4.5–5.5 V).

Logic / protocol: Single-wire, NZR serial protocol at ~800 kHz timing (one 24-bit word per pixel: G,R,B). Timing examples: T0H ≈ 0.4 µs, T1H ≈ 0.8 µs, reset (Treset) > 50 µs. 8-bit PWM per color (256 levels).

Typical current (per LED at full white): up to ~60 mA (≈20 mA per color channel) for classic WS2812B (5050). Many 3535 / “mini” variants use internal current-limiting and can show lower per-color currents (datasheet variants list values like ~12 mA per LED per color for some 3535 versions) — check the specific vendor datasheet for the exact number. Use 60 mA as a conservative design figure for full-white brightness unless your vendor datasheet states lower.
Luminous output / LEDs: depends on manufacturer / bin. Typical mini 3535 parts list various cd/m² / mcd ranges — check vendor spec for exact brightness.
Pinout: usually DIN, VDD, GND, DOUT (data in / data out chainable).
Recommended ambient / storage temps: follow the vendor datasheet (typical operating −40°C to +85°C for many parts). Verify manufacturer sheet for exact limits.
Decoupling: place a 100 µF electrolytic (or similar bulk cap) across 5 V and GND near the first LED, plus 0.1 µF bypass caps if possible. This prevents supply dips when many LEDs switch on.
Data line resistor: 220–470 Ω series resistor on the data line (between MCU and DIN) helps reduce ringing and protects the first LED. Many guides recommend it.

Level shifting: if your MCU runs at 3.3 V and LEDs at 5 V, 3.3 V data sometimes works, but a proper level shifter (or a fast MOSFET-based level translator) is recommended for reliability on long runs.

Power distribution: at full white use lots of current — inject 5 V power every ~30–50 LEDs (or according to your layout) to avoid voltage drop and color-shift. Calculate total current: I_total ≈ LEDs × I_per_LED_fullwhite (e.g. 100 LEDs × 60 mA = 6 A).
Frame/refresh rate: ~800 kHz data rate → full-frame update time depends on LED count (e.g. ~37 FPS for ~900 LEDs at 24 bits/LED theoretical). Real-world animation speed varies with controller code.

name: BL0939 Single Phase Multifunction Energy Metering IC TSSOP20

blocks.text: BL0939 is a calibration-free energy metering chip with a built-in clock. It is suitable for applications such as single-phase multi-function energy meters, smart sockets, smart home appliances, and electric bicycle charging piles. BL0939 integrates 3 high- precision Sigma-Delta ADCs , which can measure 2 currents and 1 voltage at the same time.

BL0939 can measure current, voltage RMS, active power, active energy and other parameters, and can output fast current RMS ( for leakage monitoring or overcurrent protection ) , as well as temperature detection, waveform output and other functions, output through UART/SPI interface.
Three independent Sigma-Delta ADCs for measuring two currents and one voltage.

name: ZMPT107-1 Current Type precision voltage Sensor transformer
desc: ZMPT107-1 Current Type precision voltage Sensor transformer

blocks.text: ZMPT107-1 – Precision AC Voltage Transformer / Voltage Sensor (Current-Type)
Type: Current-type AC voltage transformer (PCB-mount, epoxy-encapsulated)
Rated Input / Output Current: 2 mA → 2 mA
Turns Ratio: 1000 : 1000 (i.e. 1:1 current transformer ratio, used for voltage sensing via sampling resistor)

Linear Voltage Range: up to ~1000 V (AC mains or other high-voltage AC), with a sampling resistor (burden resistor) on the secondary to convert current to proportional voltage — 0 ~ 1000 V input → 0 ~ 10 mA secondary (with 50 Ω sampling resistor)
Linearity / Accuracy: ≤ 0.2% linearity (from ~20% to 120% of rated input)
Phase Angle Error: ≤ 45′ (minutes) when measured at rated input (2 mA primary, 50 Ω sampling resistor) — good for accurate voltage & power measurement.
Isolation (Dielectric Strength): 3000 VAC between primary (mains) and secondary — gives galvanic isolation, improving safety when interfacing with microcontrollers.
Package / Mounting: Epoxy-sealed, PCB-mount (through-hole) transformer; pin length > 3 mm for reliable soldering.
Operating Temperature Range: –40 °C to +85 °C (according to spec sheet)
Shell Material: PBT (suitable for wave soldering)
AC Voltage Measurement / Monitoring: Use to safely sense mains AC voltage (or other high-voltage AC) in systems like energy meters, power monitoring devices, automation controllers.
Galvanic Isolation: Provides isolation between high-voltage AC mains and low-voltage MCU/logic side — safer for microcontroller-based designs (Arduino, ESP32, STM32, etc.).

Voltage-to-Voltage Conversion via Current Sampling: Because it’s “current-type”: the mains voltage is effectively transformed into a small AC current on the secondary side; you need a burden resistor (sampling resistor) to convert that current to a manageable AC-voltage for ADC or measurement.
Power/Energy Meters, Voltage Regulators, Over-voltage / Under-voltage Detection, Ground-fault detection, Industrial & Household Equipment Monitoring.

name: LILYGO T-Display-S3 ESP32 WiFi and Bluetooth Development Board

blocks.text: LILYGO T-Display-S3 ESP32 WiFi and Bluetooth Development Board

The LILYGO ESP32 T-Display-S3 Development Board is a powerful 32-bit 240MHz processor with a large 16MB Flash program memory. It incorporates a 1.9″ full color LCD, 2 user buttons and has WiFi and Bluetooth capability. It packs a lot of power and functionality in a very small package.
Key Features of LILYGO ESP32 T-DISPLAY DEVELOPMENT BOARD
Display: 170 x 320 full color 1.9″ ST7789V TFT LCD. 8-bit parallel interface. Acrylic cover plate
Connector Support: STEMMA QT / Qwiic JST-SH 1.0mm 4-pin
Integrated Sensors: IR remote, Hall sensor, temperature sensor, touch sensors, pulse counter, LNA
Bluetooth: BLE 5 (Bluetooth Low Energy) + BT Mesh
Buttons: 2 user programmable buttons GPIO0 and GPIO14 + Reset
Programming: Compatible with Arduino IDE or Micropython
Pin Spacing: 0.1″ pin to pin x 0.9″ row to row. Breadboard compatible with pins installed.
Operating Voltage: 3.3V internal power and I/O.
Power Source: 5V USB, 5V VIN pin, 3.7V lithium battery

The ESP32 based T-Display-S3 is a very flexible IOT board with significant processing power. It provides 16 MB of Flash memory for program space and runs at clock speeds of 240 MHz so has a fast processing speed. Because it incorporates an LCD for user feedback and has 2 buttons for user input, it can function as a complete little standalone system right out of the box simply by connecting it to a USB cable. Because of its WiFi and Bluetooth capabilities, it can also be used as a peripheral device in conjunction with another MCU just to provide WiFi, Bluetooth or other unique capabilities that it has.

With the pins installed, the 24-pin board is breadboard compatible and will leave one row of open contacts on each side of the board for making jumper connections. Be sure when using with a solderless breadboard to insert the T-Display-S3 into the breadboard by pressing on the pins and ends of the module and do not press directly on the LCD or damage could result. The USB end of the module with connectors on the bottom should overhang the end of the breadboard for clearance.
The display is a 1.9″ IPS TFT LCD with a resolution of 170 x 320. It has an acrylic mount to help support the display and provide a more integrated package than on the base T-Display module.

Unlike most displays, this one uses an 8-bit parallel bus, so it has the potential for very fast graphic updates. The pins used to drive the LCD are dedicated and are not brought out to the edge of the module.
The display uses the ST7789V driver and is supported by the TFT-eSPI library and is also compatible with the LVGL library.

One of the main limitations of the module for some applications is the relatively small number of I/O pins, but the ESP32 chip allows most of the I/O such as the serial ports, SPI and I2C to be multiplexed to any of the other GPIO pins for maximum flexibility.

This diagram shows how the pins are used on the T-Display-S3 module. Note that some pins are used internally for driving the LCD display and as inputs for two user buttons. Those pins are not brought out to the main header pins leaving 16 pins available for the user.

There are 13 GPIO on the board that are brought out to the header pins. The pins are labeled GPIOx. When using with Arduino IDE, the digital pin number is the same as the GPIO pin number, so GPIO2 is referenced as just ‘2’.
All of the digital I/O support interrupts. In addition they can be configured to have pull-up or pull-down resistors. 9 of the pins support hardware PWM.

There are 3 pushbuttons included on the board. The two on top of the module are user programmable buttons on GPIO0 and GPIO14 which do not come out to the pins on the edge of the board. A third button on the side is a standard reset button that resets the ESP32 microprocessor.
Unlike some other development boards, the T-Display-S3 does not have a user controllable LED on any of its pins, but then again it has a complete display, so take that Arduino!
The digital I/O is limited to 3.3V. If using with 5V logic inputs, logic level translators must be used to prevent possible damage.

There are two 12-bit analog-to-digital converters (ADC1 / ADC2) on the ESP32. One or both of the A/D converters can be multiplexed across up to 10 input pins on this module. As with all the I/O pins, the analog inputs are limited to a voltage range of 0-3.3V. Higher voltages can damage the module

12-bit resolution provides readings in the range of 0-4095. The resolution of the A/D converters can be changed to a lower bit depth of 9-12 bits if desired. As with many high performance microcontrollers that have built in A/D converters on the same substrate, some amount of digital noise tends to get into the analog readings. Using a lower bit depth can help to reduce the impact of digital noise since the individual reading steps are larger.

Keep in mind that the A/D converters don’t have a completely linear behavior at the extreme ends of their range. If measuring a 0 to 3.3V voltage range, it may not be possible to differentiate between 0.0V and 0.1V or 3.2V and 3.3V so keep that in mind when interpreting the readings.
The ADC2 converter cannot be used when WiFi is also being used, in that case ADC1 should be used.

Internally GPIO4 is connected to the battery voltage and can be used to monitor the voltage level. It is connected via a divide by 2 resistor circuit, so the measured value will need to be multiplied by 2. When USB power is connected, this pin will measure the USB voltage, not the battery voltage.
The module has the standard built-in buses and in many cases arbitrary GPIO pins can be assigned to those buses.

The CD4067BM is a CMOS 16-channel analog multiplexer/demultiplexer.
It allows one of sixteen analog or digital input/output lines to be connected to a common output/input line.
The channel selection is controlled by 4 binary address lines, and an enable pin allows easy control of the connection state.
It is ideal for analog signal routing, sensor selection, or data acquisition systems.

blocks.text: CS1237 24 bit analog-to-digital ADC converter IC SMD SOP8
The CS1237 is a high-precision, low-power 24-bit Δ-Σ (delta-sigma) ADC designed for measuring small analog signals such as load cells, pressure sensors, and other bridge-type sensors.
It integrates a programmable gain amplifier (PGA), voltage reference, oscillator, and control logic in a compact SOP-8 package, minimizing external component requirements.
It is ideal for weighing scales, industrial sensors, and data acquisition systems requiring high accuracy and low noise.

blocks.v: VREF · Voltage reference input/output (internal 2.5V reference output)
DOUT · Data output (serial data ready signal)
XIN · External clock input (leave open for internal oscillator)

blocks.text: The CS1237 continuously samples the differential input voltage (AIN+ – AIN–) using a Δ-Σ modulator, followed by a digital filter.
Data is output through the DOUT pin using a clock from PD_SCK, similar to the HX711 interface.
When PD_SCK is held high for >1 ms, the device enters power-down mode.
The gain and sampling rate are selectable through internal registers or configuration programming.
Equivalent / Similar Devices: HX711, CS1238, NAU7802
Use low-noise differential input wiring for sensors.

If using an external reference, tie VREF to your reference source.
When using the internal reference, bypass VREF with 1 µF to GND.

The codes given in the chart below usually tell the length and width of the components in tenths of millimeters or hundredths of inches. Problematically, some manufacturers are developing metric 0201 components with dimensions of 0.25 mm × 0.125 mm (0.0098 in × 0.0049 in), but the imperial 01005 name is already being used for the 0.4 mm × 0.2 mm (0.0157 in × 0.0079 in) package.

name: RP2040-Zero Raspberry Pi MCU Development Board

blocks.text: RP2040-Zero Raspberry Pi MCU Development Board
264kB on-chip SRAM in six independent banks
Support for up to 16MB of off-chip Flash memory via dedicated QSPI bus
On-chip programmable LDO to generate core voltage
2 on-chip PLLs to generate USB and core clocks
30 GPIO pins, 4 of which can be used as analog inputs
USB 1.1 controller and PHY, with host and device support

Inside the RP2040 is a ‘permanent ROM’ USB UF2 bootloader. What that means is when you want to program new firmware, you can hold down the BOOTSEL button while plugging it into USB (or pulling down the RUN/Reset pin to ground) and it will appear as a USB disk drive you can drag the firmware onto. Just note you don’t double-click reset, instead hold down BOOTSEL during boot to enter the bootloader!

The RP2040 is a powerful chip, which has the clock speed of (SAMD51), and two cores that are equivalent to M0 (SAMD21). Since it is an M0 chip, it does not have a floating point unit or DSP hardware support – so if you’re doing something with heavy floating point math, it will be done in software and thus not as fast as an M4. For many other computational tasks, you’ll get close-to-M4 speeds!

For peripherals, there are two I2C controllers, two SPI controllers, and two UARTs that are multiplexed across the GPIO – check the pinout for what pins can be set to which. There are 16 PWM channels, each pin has a channel it can be set to (ditto on the pinout).

You’ll note there’s no I2S peripheral, or SDIO, or camera, what’s up with that? Well instead of having specific hardware support for serial-data-like peripherals like these, the RP2040 comes with the PIO state machine system which is a unique and powerful way to create custom hardware logic and data processing blocks that run on their own without taking up a CPU. For example, NeoPixels – often we bitbang the timing-specific protocol for these LEDs. For the RP2040, we instead use PIO object that reads in the data buffer and clocks out the right bitstream with perfect accuracy. Same with I2S audio in or out, LED matrix displays, 8-bit or SPI based TFTs, even VGA! In MicroPython and CircuitPython you can create PIO control commands to script the peripheral and load it in at runtime. There are 2 PIO peripherals with 4 state machines each.

While the RP2040 has lots of onboard RAM (264KB), it does not have built-in FLASH memory. Instead, that is provided by the external QSPI flash chip. You will need to provide external FLASH memory using QSPI NOR memory. The flash chip is shared between the program it’s running and any file storage used by MicroPython or CircuitPython.

name: PCB For DIY Line Tracking Car
desc: PCB For DIY Line Tracking Car

blocks.text: PCB For DIY Line Tracking Car
a DIY simple line-Tracking and obstacle-avoiding car, requiring the use of digital circuits to implement the tracking function and analog circuits to implement the obstacle avoidance function.

According to the design requirements, a 74HC00N NAND gate is used in conjunction with an infrared emitting tube. By judging whether infrared light is detected, the receiving tube is turned on or not, and the signal is input into the NAND gate to realize digital circuit tracking.

Using the LM393 comparator with the infrared emitting tube, it is also to determine whether the infrared light is detected in front and whether the receiving tube is turned on. The two sets of signals are input into the comparator for comparison to realize the obstacle avoidance function of the analog circuit.

The device is powered by two AA batteries, each with a voltage of 1.5V. Connecting two batteries in series provides a voltage of 3V, meeting the chip’s minimum power requirements. A three-position slide switch allows for switching between tracking and obstacle avoidance functions. Capacitors C1 and C3 are filter capacitors for energy storage. When the motor starts operating, transient currents are high, and the 100uF capacitor helps discharge the batteries.

The positive pole of the battery is connected to the positive pole of the motor, and the negative pole is controlled and turned on through a transistor. When a digital tracking or analog obstacle avoidance signal is generated, the base of the transistor is controlled to control the operation of the left and right tires, thereby realizing the tracking and obstacle avoidance functions.
U2 and U3 are infrared emitting tubes, and LED3 and LED4 are corresponding infrared receiving tubes, which are installed on both sides of the front wheels. The principle analysis is as follows:

When the car starts to move and hits the white paper, the infrared light is reflected and received by the receiving tube, which turns on. When it hits the black line, the infrared light is absorbed and the receiving tube turns off.
74HC00N is a NAND gate. When it touches the black line, the receiving tube is cut off, CNT1 outputs a high level, corresponding to OUT1 outputs a low level, and OUT3 outputs a high level;
At this time, the high level output by OUT3 will flow through the motor transistor, controlling the three-stage conduction and the motor rotation;
The vehicle continuously encounters black and white lines on the map route, thereby continuously turning on and off the transistor, realizing the line patrol function around the black line track.

IR1 and IR2 are infrared transmitting tubes, and CGQ1 and CGQ2 are corresponding infrared receiving tubes, which are installed on both sides of the front of the vehicle. The schematic diagram is analyzed as follows:

When the vehicle is running, there is no obstacle in front, the infrared transmission signal will not be received, the receiving tube is cut off, the 393 comparator’s non-inverting input terminal is the battery voltage, and the voltage is greater than the inverting input terminal. At this time, the 393 comparator outputs a high level to control the vehicle to move forward.

When there is an obstacle in front of the car, the infrared emission signal is received by the receiving tube, the receiving tube is turned on, 393 is relatively strong, the same-direction input end is low level, and the voltage is less than the inverting input end. At this time, 393 comparator outputs a low level, the corresponding wheel stops running, thereby achieving steering.

The TPL5110DDCR is a nano-power system timer from Texas Instruments, ideal for ultra-low-power applications like power gating in battery-powered or duty-cycled systems. Here are its core specs:
Supply Voltage: Operates from 1.8 V to 5.5 V
Typical Operating Current: 35 nA at 2.5 V

Selection Method: By adjusting resistor values (resistor-selectable interval)

Includes a MOSFET driver to gate power (acts as a power switch)
Intended Use Cases: Designed for battery-powered systems, IoT nodes, intruder or tamper detection, home automation sensors, thermostats, remote sensors, and more
The TPL5110DDCR acts like an ultra-efficient timer-based switch:
You set it to wake up your main system (like a microcontroller) at intervals ranging from a fraction of a second to two hours.
When the timer fires, the built-in MOSFET driver activates power (turns on) to your system.
Optionally, you can use “one-shot” mode to briefly power up only once.
After the job is done (e.g., taking a measurement or transmitting data), your system can signal the TPL5110 to turn itself off again, consuming virtually no standby power (just 35 nA!).

name: UT123D Smart Digital Multimeter
desc: UT123D Smart Digital Multimeter The UT123D Smart Digital Multimeter by UNI-T is a compact, True RMS multimeter designed for accurate voltage, current, resistance, and capacitance measurements. It features auto-ranging , non-contact voltage detection (NCV) , a backlit display with a bar graph , and a data hold function. Rated for CAT III 600V , it is ideal for both residential and commercial electrical testing, offering safety, reliability, and ease of use in various environments. Perfect for professionals and hobbyists alike.

blocks.text: The UT123D Smart Digital Multimeter from UNI-T is a compact, feature-rich tool designed for both professionals and hobbyists who need a versatile, reliable multimeter for electrical measurement.
Provides accurate readings for both AC and DC signals, even with non-sinusoidal waveforms, ensuring reliable performance in all electrical environments.

The multimeter automatically selects the appropriate range for voltage, current, resistance, capacitance, and other parameters, simplifying the testing process and eliminating the need for manual range selection.

The UT123D includes built-in NCV functionality, which allows users to detect the presence of live wires or voltage without direct contact. It features both visual (LED) and audible alerts for added safety.
Large, Backlit Display with Bar Graph:

The large, easy-to-read backlit LCD screen (4000-count) enhances readability in low-light conditions. The display includes a bar graph, which helps to monitor dynamic changes in electrical readings in real time.

The multimeter features a data hold function, allowing users to freeze the displayed value for later reference. It also includes a continuity buzzer, which is particularly useful for quickly identifying open circuits.

The UT123D is designed to be rugged, compact, and lightweight, making it ideal for use in tight spaces, fieldwork, or on-the-go measurements. Its durable construction ensures it withstands everyday wear and tear.
Rated for CAT III 600V, the UT123D complies with stringent safety standards to protect both the user and the device from electrical surges and potential overloads.
The device operates on two AAA batteries, ensuring long-lasting performance. An automatic power-off function helps conserve battery life when not in use.
Display: 4000-count, 44mm x 26mm EBTN LCD with bar graph.

The UT123D is ideal for electrical contractors and technicians working in residential and commercial installations. It is perfect for testing circuits, motors, appliances, and other electrical systems.
It is also widely used in automotive maintenance for diagnosing electrical components like batteries, alternators, and circuits.
The UT123D offers an easy-to-use interface for hobbyists and electronics enthusiasts working with circuits, sensors, and other low-voltage electronics.

blocks.text: ESP32-C6 is Espressif’s first WiFi 6 SoC integrating 2.4 GHz WiFi 6, Bluetooth 5 (LE) and the 802.15.4 protocol. It features an industry-leading RF performance, with reliable security features and multiple memory resources for IoT products. It consists of a high-performance (HP) 32-bit RISC-V processor, which can be clocked up to 160 MHz and a low-power (LP) 32-bit RISC-V processor, which can be clocked up to 20 MHz. It has a 320KB ROM, a 512KB SRAM, and works with external flash. It comes with 30 (QFN40) or 22 (QFN32) programmable GPIOs, with support for SPI, UART, I2C, I2S, RMT, TWAI, PWM, SDIO, Motor Control PWM. It also packs a 12-bit ADC and a temperature sensor.

The ESP32-C6 has integrated 2.4 GHz WiFi 6 (802.11ax) radio, and also supports the 802.11b/g/n standard for backward compatibility. ESP32-C6 supports the OFDMA mechanism for both uplink and downlink communications, while also supporting MU-MIMO for downlink traffic. Both of these techniques allow working with high efficiency and low latency, even in congested wireless environments. It also combines 2.4 GHz WiFi (802.11 b/g/n/ax), Bluetooth 5 (LE), and IEEE 802.15.4 radio connectivity, which is vital for making the Thread and Zigbee protocols available in a variety of cases of application development.

The ESP32-C6’s support for IEEE 802.15.4 and Wi-Fi radios, along with Bluetooth 5 (LE) connectivity, enable customers to build Matter-compliant Wi-Fi end-point devices and Thread end-point devices, thus achieving interoperability in smart-home devices from multiple brands.

RCD Phase Switch (0°/180°): Allows testing RCD trip times starting at different points in the AC cycle. Benefit: Ensures comprehensive testing of RCD performance under various conditions.

blocks.text: Industrial-Grade USB to RS422 Converter Module – CH340 & SIT3490EESA

Bridge the gap between your USB-equipped computer and robust RS422 industrial devices with this high-performance Converter Module. Engineered with the reliable CH340 USB-to-UART bridge and the noise-immune SIT3490EESA RS422 transceiver, this adapter ensures dependable serial communication in demanding industrial, automation, and embedded environments. Its dual output options, coupled with built-in protection features and debugging capabilities, make it an indispensable tool for seamless RS422 connectivity.
USB to RS422 Key Features & Benefits
Benefit: Effortlessly converts USB UART signals to balanced RS422 differential signals, ensuring reliable data transmission.
Benefit: Utilizes the industry-proven CH340 for stable USB-to-UART conversion and the SIT3490EESA transceiver for superior noise immunity and long-distance communication.
Benefit: Offers flexible connectivity with both a convenient screw terminal block for secure wiring and an RJ45 connector for standard industrial interfaces.
Benefit: Provides clear LED indicators for transmit (TX) and receive (RX) signals, allowing for easy monitoring of data flow and troubleshooting.
Benefit: Integrated Transient Voltage Suppressor (TVS) diodes on the RS422 signal lines protect your equipment from voltage spikes and electrostatic discharge (ESD).
Benefit: Features PTC (Positive Temperature Coefficient) resettable fuses on all four RS422 data lines, safeguarding against overcurrent conditions and preventing potential damage.
Benefit: Includes a dedicated header with a selectable jumper, allowing direct access to the raw UART signals before RS422 conversion for simplified debugging and signal analysis.
Wide Baud Rate Support (Up to 1 Mbps):
Benefit: Accommodates a broad range of serial communication speeds, ensuring compatibility with various RS422 devices.
Benefit: Draws power directly from the USB port (5V), eliminating the need for an external power supply and simplifying setup.
Benefit: Its small form factor allows for easy integration into various setups, while its robust design ensures reliability in demanding industrial environments.
Benefit: Ensures compatibility with older USB standards, providing flexibility in connecting to different computer systems.
USB Interface: USB 2.0 (Backward compatible with USB 1.1)
RS422 Output Connectors: Screw Terminal Block, RJ45 Connector
Overcurrent Protection: PTC Resettable Fuses (on all four RS422 lines)
Debugging Interface: Header with Jumper for UART Selection

Industrial Automation: Connecting RS422-based controllers, sensors, and Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs).
Embedded Systems Development: Interfacing with microcontrollers such as STM32, Arduino, and Raspberry Pi for robust serial communication.
Long-Distance Serial Communication: Enabling reliable data transmission over extended cable lengths in noisy environments.
CNC Machines & Motion Control: Facilitating dependable data exchange within industrial machinery and motion control systems.

Connect to Your Computer: Plug the USB connector of the module into an available USB port on your computer. The necessary drivers for the CH340 chip should automatically install on most operating systems. If not, you may need to download and install them manually.

Screw Terminal Block: Connect the RS422 A+, B-, Y+, and Z- signals from your device to the corresponding terminals on the module’s screw terminal block. Ensure correct wiring according to the RS422 standard.
RJ45 Connector: Connect a standard Ethernet cable (CAT5 or higher) from the RJ45 port of the module to the RJ45 port of your RS422 device, ensuring the pinout is compatible.

Select UART Output (Optional Debugging): If you need to access the raw UART signals for debugging, use the jumper on the debugging header to select the output to the header instead of the RS422 transceiver.

Configure Your Software: In your communication software or application, select the virtual COM port assigned to the USB-to-Serial adapter and configure the appropriate baud rate, data bits, parity, and stop bits to match the settings of your RS422 device.
Begin Communication: You can now begin sending and receiving data between your computer and the RS422 device. Monitor the TX and RX LEDs on the module to observe data transmission.

The OBD CAN Bus Shield is a compact and powerful add-on designed for ESP32 30-pin development boards, enabling automotive diagnostics, OBD-II communication, and CAN bus data monitoring. This shield is compatible with SavvyCAN, ESP32RET, and Arduino CAN bus libraries (such as Arduino TWI), making it ideal for vehicle diagnostics, reverse engineering, and embedded CAN bus projects.

blocks.text: Surface-mount components are usually smaller than their counterparts with leads, and are designed to be handled by machines rather than by humans. The electronics industry has standardized package shapes and sizes (the leading standardisation body is JEDEC). These include:

The codes given in the chart below usually tell the length and width of the components in tenths of millimeters or hundredths of inches. For example, a metric 2520 component is 2.5 mm by 2.0 mm which corresponds roughly to .10 inches by .08 inches (hence, imperial size is 1008). Exceptions occur for imperial in the two smallest rectangular passive sizes. The metric codes still represent the dimensions in mm, even though the imperial size codes are no longer aligned. Problematically, some manufacturers are developing metric 0201 components with dimensions of 0.25 mm × 0.125 mm (0.0098 in × 0.0049 in), but the imperial 01005 name is already being used for the 0.4 mm × 0.2 mm (0.0157 in × 0.0079 in) package.

The clamp-on ground testing technique provided by the Fluke 1630 simplifies ground loop testing and enables non-intrusive leakage current measurement without breaking the circuit. Its compact and rugged design makes the Fluke 1630 easy to use in small places and harsh environments. Handy features like “display hold” and continuity testing with an audible alarm, ensures additional convenience.

The Fluke 1630 uses the stakeless testing method, which eliminates the need to disconnect parallel ground rods and find suitable locations for placing auxiliary ground stakes. This saves time and enables users such as industrial and utility electricians, and field service electricians and contractors, to perform earth ground loop tests in locations where it is not possible to use other techniques, such as inside buildings or on power pylons. With the stakeless testing method, earth ground stakes are no longer necessary. The Fluke 1630 Earth Ground Clamp is clamped around the earth ground rod or the connecting cable. A known voltage is induced by one half of the clamp and the current is measured by the other half. The tester automatically determines the ground loop resistance at this grounding connection.

blocks.text: MPXV7002DP Analog Airspeed Sensor Breakout For APM

CJMCU APM2.5 MPXV7002DP Airspeed Pressure Sensor Module [5V] is a modern airspeed pressure sensor module which is based on MPXV7002 progressive integrated silicon pressure sensor chip. This chip is a piezoresistive transducer in a small space packaged. This is developed for many applications and specialized for Arduino boards, microcontroller or microprocessor projects with A/D inputs. This sensor is a precision, high-level analog output, which is proportional to the applied pressure.

MPXV7002 sensor can measure positive and negative pressure. Besides, by applying an offset particularly with 2.5V as a conventional zero, it is possible to measure to a maximum pressure of 7kPa via a single port to sense pressure and vacuum (for more information, refer to the transfer function in the datasheet). This module can be embedded on Arduplane as an airspeed sensor, to help for slow flighting and independent landing in the unstable wind conditions.

blocks.text: Using the WCH DAP Link with the STM32F103C8 microcontroller and Keil IDE is straightforward. Below is a step-by-step guide to help you set it up and start debugging/programming your STM32F103C8:
Connect the WCH DAP Link V2 to your STM32F103C8:
Connect the SWDIO pin of the WCH DAP Link V2 to the SWDIO pin (PA13) of the STM32F103C8.
Connect the SWCLK pin of the WCH DAP Link V2 to the SWCLK pin (PA14) of the STM32F103C8.
Connect the GND pin of the WCH DAP Link V2 to the GND pin of the STM32F103C8.
Connect the 3.3V pin of the WCH DAP Link V2 to the 3.3V pin of the STM32F103C8 (if needed for power).
Connect the WCH DAP Link to your PC:
Use the USB-C cable to connect the WCH DAP Link to your computer.
If you haven’t already, download and install the latest version of Keil µVision IDE from the Keil website.
Open Keil IDE and go to Pack Installer (click the puzzle piece icon or navigate via Project > Manage > Pack Installer).
Search for STM32F1 Series Device Family Pack and install it.
Install WCH DAP Link Drivers (if required):
Most operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS) will recognize the WCH DAP Link V2 automatically. If not, download the drivers from the WCH website.
Step 3: Configure Keil IDE for WCH DAP Link
Open Keil IDE and create a new project or open an existing one for the STM32F103C8.
Go to Project > Options for Target (or press Alt + F7).
Select CMSIS-DAP Debugger from the dropdown menu under “Use.”
Click on Settings next to the debugger dropdown.
In the Debug tab, ensure the following:
Ensure the Reset and Run option is checked.
Add the STM32F1xx Flash algorithm (it should be available if you installed the STM32F1 device pack).
Click on Verify in the debug settings to ensure the WCH DAP Link is properly connected to the STM32F103C8.
Step 4: Build and Flash the Firmware
Click on Build (or press F7) to compile your project.
Click on Download (or press F8) to flash the firmware to the STM32F103C8.
Click on Debug (or press Ctrl + F5) to start a debugging session.
Use Keil’s debugging tools (breakpoints, watch windows, etc.) to debug your code.
Click on Run (or press F5) to execute the program on the STM32F103C8.

name: WS2811 SMD LED power driver IC SOP8
desc: WS2811 SMD LED power driver IC SOP8

blocks.text: WS2811 SMD LED power driver IC SOP8
 Output port compression 20V. DIN port compression 9.5V.
 Built-in voltage-regulator tube, only a resistance needed to add to IC VDD feet when under 24V power supply.
 256 Gray-scale adjustable and scan frequency is more than 2KHz.
 Built in signal reshaping circuit, to ensure
The WS2811 is 3 output channels special for LED driver circuit. Its internal includes intelligent digital port data latch
and signal reshaping amplification drive circuit. Also include a precision internal oscillator and a 12V voltage
programmable constant current output drive. In the purpose of reduce power supply ripple, the 3 output channels
IC use single NZR communication mode. After the chip power-on reset, the DIN port receive data from controller, the
first IC collect initial 24bit data then sent to the internal data latch, the other data which reshaping by the internal signal
reshaping amplification circuit sent to the next cascade IC through the DO port. After transmission for each chip, the
signal to reduce 24bit. IC adopt auto reshaping transmit technology, making the chip cascade number is not limited the
signal transmission, only depend on the speed of signal transmission.
The data latch of IC depend on the received 24bit data produce different duty ratio signal at OUTR, OUTG, OUTB
port. All chip synchronous send the received data to each segment when the DIN port input a reset signal. It will receive
new data again After the reset signal finished. Before a new reset signal received, the control signal of OUTR ,OUTG,
OUTB port unchanged. IC sent PWM data that received justly to OUTR, OUTG, OUTB port, after receive a low voltage

blocks.text: Fluke 435-II Power Quality and Energy Analyzers
Analyze power quality issues, calculate the costs of wasted energy and prevent downtime with the Fluke 434-II Energy Analyzer and Fluke 435-II Power Quality and Energy Analyzer.
Fluke 435-II Power Quality and Energy Analyzers
Product overview: Fluke 434-II and 435-II Power Quality and Energy Analyzers

The Fluke 434-II Energy Analyzer and 435-II Power Quality and Energy Analyzer are designed to help you minimize downtime, quickly troubleshoot power quality issues and easily discover the costs of wasted energy. Downtime is expensive and getting the data you need to solve to critical power quality problems quickly is key. The 434-II and 435-II Analyzer’s measurement process and data output have been optimized to help you access the most critical information easily.

Multiple parameters are measured simultaneously and displayed in formats that quickly describe overall power quality health. The detailed information helps you make better maintenance decisions—whether you’re trying to reduce energy waste, find the source of power quality issues or see how motor startups are affecting your electrical system. Data can be accessed as simple digital values, trend graphs (for fast insight into changes over time), waveforms, or phasor diagrams. The data can also be analyzed and organized into tabular formats. Detailed event data allows you to see the magnitude, duration and time stamping of anomalies enabling you to rapidly correlate the problems you are experiencing in your facility.
Energy Loss Calculator—Calculate money lost to energy waste in terms of real dollars.
Fluke 430 Series II Energy Loss Calculator

It’s a simple fact, poor power quality can have a big impact on the bottom line. The Fluke 434-II Energy Analyzer and Fluke 435-II Power Quality and Energy Analyzer enable you to identify issues and measure energy loss giving you specific insight into the amount of loss in dollars. The Energy Loss Calculator helps you better understand your energy consumption by creating associations between things like effective power and poor power quality characteristics such as reactive power, unbalance, distortion, or neutral current. These power quality and energy analyzers also offer users the flexibility to input cable length and diameter to calculate loss due to conductor sizing (or use AUTO mode if cable specifications are unknown) and enter up to four unique time-dependent daily rates (kWh) for more accurate calculations. Armed with this critical data, users can easily justify the investment necessary to take countermeasures.
Advanced Power Quality Health—At-a-glance power quality health data in real-time so you have the data you need, when you need it

The Fluke 434-II Energy Analyzer and 435-II Power Quality and Energy Analyzer utilize an integrated Power Quality Health summary that gives you an at-a-glance view of a complete range of power quality issues in real time. With a simple graphical presentation, complete with tolerance limits, you can quickly discover which power quality problems may be present on your electrical system. If you don’t know where to start or what problems might exist, the advanced Power Quality Health summary simplifies the task and serves as a comprehensive starting point for further troubleshooting.

Power inverters take dc current and transform it into ac current, or vice versa. But, what percentage of that power going into the inverter comes out as usable current? The Fluke 434-II and 435-II Analyzers have an integrated power inverter efficiency mode that allows users to better understand power inverter performance. Nothing is ever 100 % efficient, and a power inverter’s efficiency will vary depending on how much power is being used at the time (with the efficiency generally being greater when more power is being used). Inverters can also lose performance over time and need to be checked. By comparing the input power with the output power, you can determine the system efficiency. With the Power Inverter Efficiency feature you can discover just how good your inverter is at converting your dc power to ac (or vice versa).
AutoTrend capability shows changes over time

With a unique AutoTrend feature you can get fast insight into power quality changes over time. Every displayed reading is automatically and continuously recorded without having to set up threshold levels or having to manually start the process so you can quickly view trends in voltage, current, frequency, power, harmonics or flicker on all three phases plus neutral.

Power quality issues can affect the operation of critical loads and have a negative impact on your bottom line. Think of the Fluke 435-II Power Quality and Energy Analyzer as your insurance policy. Calculate the cost of wasted energy due to poor power quality and troubleshoot the source of power quality or motor performance issues all with a single test tool designed to give you the data you need to quickly get to the root of the problem.
Wrapped in a lightweight, rugged package, the Fluke 434-II Energy Analyzer and 435-II Power Quality and Energy Analyzer are the ideal portable power quality instruments.

blocks.text: Versatile AVR Development Board for ATmega16/ATmega32 with USB-UART & ISP

Unlock the potential of 40-pin AVR microcontrollers like the ATmega32 and ATmega16 with this comprehensive development board. Designed for seamless prototyping, programming, and testing, this board caters to both beginners venturing into the world of AVR and experienced users tackling advanced projects. Its integrated features streamline the development process, offering convenience and flexibility in one robust package.
Benefit: Provides both USB-to-UART communication for serial debugging and AVR ISP (In-System Programming) capability, simplifying code uploading and interaction.
Benefit: Easily toggle between USB-to-UART mode (for serial communication) and ISP programming mode with a dedicated switch, ensuring the correct configuration for your task.

Benefit: Seamlessly integrates with the Arduino IDE when used with the MightyCore board definition, granting access to the vast Arduino library ecosystem and numerous code examples for AVR microcontrollers.

Benefit: In UART mode, the RTS pin is intelligently connected to the microcontroller’s reset pin, enabling automatic reset functionality during Arduino IDE uploads – a familiar and convenient workflow.
Benefit: Allows for effortless insertion and removal of 40-pin AVR microcontrollers without the risk of pin damage, making it ideal for experimentation and iterative development.

Benefit: Offers a DC power jack (accepting 7-15V input) and onboard 5V (78M05) and 3.3V (LD1117-3.3) voltage regulators, providing stable power for your microcontroller and accessible headers for powering external peripherals.
Benefit: Ensures accurate and reliable timing for your microcontroller applications with the integrated 16MHz crystal oscillator.
Easy Peripheral Connectivity via GPIO Headers:

Benefit: All General Purpose Input/Output (GPIO) pins of the microcontroller are conveniently broken out to male headers, facilitating easy connection to sensors, actuators, and other external circuits.
Benefit: Features 3 general-purpose LEDs and 3 push buttons directly connected to microcontroller pins, enabling quick testing of digital outputs and inputs without the need for external components.
Benefit: Provides a readily accessible reset button for manually restarting your microcontroller during development and testing.
Supported Microcontrollers: ATmega16, ATmega32, and other 40-pin AVR microcontrollers
GPIO Access: All GPIO pins brought out to male headers
Arduino Compatibility: Yes, via MightyCore board definition

Install Arduino IDE and MightyCore: Download and install the Arduino IDE. Then, install the MightyCore board definition following the instructions on the MightyCore GitHub page to add support for ATmega16/32 and other compatible AVR microcontrollers.

Connect the Board: Connect the development board to your computer using a USB cable. Ensure the mode selection switch is in the desired position (UART for Arduino IDE upload, ISP for direct ISP programming).
Select Board and Port in Arduino IDE: In the Arduino IDE, under the “Tools” menu, select the appropriate board (e.g., ATmega32) and the correct serial port corresponding to your board.
Write and Upload Code: Write your Arduino sketches and upload them to the microcontroller. If the switch is in UART mode, the automatic reset feature should initiate the upload process.

Experiment with Peripherals: Connect external components to the GPIO headers, utilize the onboard LEDs and push buttons for basic testing, and explore the capabilities of your chosen AVR microcontroller.

ISP Programming (Alternative): For direct ISP programming, ensure the mode selection switch is in the ISP position and use a compatible ISP programmer (if the CH340 doesn’t handle ISP for your specific setup, you might need an external programmer connected to the ICSP header if present on the board – consult the board’s specific documentation).

blocks.text: Alpha Plus board Arduino Uno Compatible for Robotics Development and DIY Projects

The UGE Alpha PLUS is an enhanced, Arduino UNO-compatible development board designed for DIY robotics and other creative projects. Built around the ATMega328P microcontroller with an UNO bootloader, it integrates various peripherals to save time and maximize productivity. The onboard CH340C USB-to-UART chip facilitates seamless code uploading and serial communication.
USB Interface: CH340C for easy code uploads and communication.
Power Options: USB, 7-12V DC Terminal Connector, or DC Jack.
Motor Control: Built-in L293DD dual motor driver for two motors plus an auxiliary motor.
Connectivity: Bluetooth, NRF24L01, I2C/OLED headers, and dedicated sensor headers (ultrasonic, IR, flame, servo).
IR Receiver: 38KHz with jumper for connection control.
Pin Headers: Rich analog and digital headers with power pins.
Power Options: Equipped with DC jack and terminal block for flexible power input, with reverse polarity protection via a diode. A 78M05 regulator supplies stable current.
USB to UART: Built-in CH340C USB-to-UART converter with TX/RX indicator LEDs for programming ease.
Arduino UNO Compatibility: Same form factor and female headers as the Arduino UNO, ensuring shield compatibility while managing shared pins for onboard peripherals.
Easy Sensor Connections: All ATmega328 GPIO pins are routed to color-coded male headers with Signal, VCC, and GND, allowing easy sensor connections without expansion shields.
Configurable Buzzer: Buzzer connected to D2 with a jumper, allowing enable/disable functionality.
Infrared (IR) Receiver: 38kHz IR receiver on A2 with a jumper for connection control.
OLED Display Header: 4-pin header for OLED display on A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL) for I2C.
Bluetooth Module Header: 4-pin header for HC-05 Bluetooth module on D0 (RX) and D1 (TX). Remove during programming to avoid UART conflict.
Dual DC Motor Driver: L293DD motor driver for two DC motors.
Motor Speed Control: EN1 (D3) for Motor1 and EN2 (D5) for Motor2 using PWM with analogWrite().
Motor Direction Control: Motor1 direction via D6 and Motor2 direction via D7, with NOT gate logic to save pins.

Auxiliary Motor Driver Output: A medium-power NPN transistor is connected to D2 (shared with the buzzer) for driving auxiliary DC loads (motors, pumps, solenoids, lamps). A dedicated 2-pin jumper enables/disables the output.
NRF24L01 Wireless Header: Header for NRF24L01 wireless transceiver module, enabling wireless communication with other boards or RC remotes that use the NRF24 module.

UGE Alpha PLUS is perfect for makers, hobbyists, and students working on robotics, automation, and IoT projects. The board’s extensive peripheral support allows for quick prototyping and flexible integration of various modules and sensors. Whether controlling motors, reading sensor data, or adding wireless connectivity, UGE UNO PLUS offers a versatile platform for a wide range of creative applications.
UGE UNO PLUS Getting Started Guide
Download and install the latest version of the Arduino IDE from the official website.
Ensure that the CH340C driver is installed to allow communication between your UGE UNO PLUS and your computer. The driver can be found here for different operating systems.
Use a USB cable to connect your UGE Alpha PLUS to your computer.
The board can also be powered via the DC Jack (7-12V) or the Terminal Connector if needed.
Go to Tools > Board and select “Arduino Uno.”
Go to Tools > Port and choose the appropriate COM port for your board.
In the Arduino IDE, go to File > Examples > Basics > Blink.
Click the “Upload” button to upload the sketch to your board.
The onboard LED (usually connected to pin 13) should start blinking.
Motor Control: Connect motors to the L293DD motor driver terminals, and use the relevant Arduino pins (as per the onboard labeling) to control motor speed and direction.
Bluetooth: Attach a Bluetooth module to the dedicated 4-pin header. Use the UART pins for communication (TX/RX).
IR Remote: The IR receiver is connected to a specific digital pin. Include the IRremote library in your sketch to use this feature.
Sensors: Connect sensors to the dedicated 3-pin headers (GND-VCC-SIG) and use corresponding analog/digital pins in your sketches.
Connect an OLED display or any I2C device to the 4-pin I2C header.
Use the Wire library for I2C communication.
Plug the NRF24L01 module into the dedicated header.
Use the RF24 library to communicate with other NRF24L01 devices.
Write your own Arduino code or modify existing examples to suit your project.
Test the code by uploading and monitoring the serial output using the Arduino IDE’s Serial Monitor.
The board includes an onboard AMS1117 LDO regulator providing 3.3V. Ensure your peripherals do not exceed the 800mA limit.
Experiment with controlling the onboard buzzer and IR receiver via their respective jumpers.
Use the available pin headers for quick prototyping and sensor integration.

name: Crystal Oscillator 2Pin HC-49S 8MHZ
desc: Crystal Oscillator 2Pin HC-49S 8MHZ

blocks.text: A quartz crystal provides both series and parallel resonance. The series resonance is a few kilohertz lower than the parallel one. Crystals below 30 MHz are generally operated between series and parallel resonance, which means that the crystal appears as an inductive reactance in operation, this inductance forming a parallel resonant circuit with externally connected parallel capacitance. Any small additional capacitance in parallel with the crystal will thus pull the frequency downwards. Moreover, the effective inductive reactance of the crystal can be reduced by adding a capacitor in series with the crystal. This latter technique can provide a useful method of trimming the oscillatory frequency within a narrow range; in this case inserting a capacitor in series with the crystal will raise the frequency of oscillation. For a crystal to operate at its specified frequency, the electronic circuit has to be exactly that specified by the crystal manufacturer. Note that these points imply a subtlety concerning crystal oscillators in this frequency range: the crystal does not usually oscillate at precisely either of its resonant frequencies.

Crystals above 30 MHz (up to >200 MHz) are generally operated at series resonance where the impedance appears at its minimum and equal to the series resistance. For these crystals the series resistance is specified (<100 Ω) instead of the parallel capacitance. To reach higher frequencies, a crystal can be made to vibrate at one of its overtone modes, which occur near multiples of the fundamental resonant frequency. Only odd numbered overtones are used. Such a crystal is referred to as a 3rd, 5th, or even 7th overtone crystal. To accomplish this, the oscillator circuit usually includes additional LC circuits to select the desired overtone.

name: 1 Channel 12V Solid State Relay Active Low SSR Module

blocks.text: A solid state relay (SSR) is just what it sounds like; an IC that acts like a mechanical relay. They allow you to control high-voltage AC loads from lower voltage DC control circuitry. They accomplish this by using infrared light as the ‘contact,’ a solid-state relay SSR is really just an IR LED and a phototriac sealed up into a little box.

Solid state relays, have several advantages over mechanical relays. One such advantage is that they can be switched by a much lower voltage and at a much lower current than most mechanical relays. Also, because there’s no moving contacts, solid state relays can be switched much faster and for much longer periods without wearing out.
Input voltage: 12VDC, Maximum Output Current: 2A, Maximum Output Voltage: 240VAC
Input Voltage of Control Signal: 0-2.5V (low level state), the relay will be on; 3-5V (high level state), the relay will be off.
DC+: Connected to positive supply voltage (supply power according to relay voltage)
DC-: Connected to negative supply voltage
CH1:Signal triggering terminal of relay module
The meaning of high and low level:

Triggered at high level means a forward voltage exists between signal triggering terminal (CH1) and negative supply voltage. It generally connects positive supply voltage and triggering terminal together. When triggering terminal has positive supply voltage or reaches triggering voltage, the relay will pull in.

While triggered at low level means the voltage between the signal triggering terminal (CH1) and negative supply voltage is 0V, or the voltage at the triggering terminal is lower than positive supply voltage. If it lowers to a triggering voltage, the relay will pull in. It generally connects negative supply voltage and triggering terminal together.

blocks.text: When a low level is supplied to signal terminal of the solid state relay, the LED at the output terminal will light up. Otherwise, it will turn off. If a periodic high and low level is supplied to the signal terminal, you can see the LED will cycle between on and off.

// the setup function runs once when you press reset or power the board

The Cortex-M4 core features a single-precision floating-point unit (FPU), which supports all the Arm single-precision data-processing instructions and all the data types. The devices also embed several protection mechanisms for embedded Flash memory and SRAM: readout protection, write protection, securable memory area and proprietary code readout protection.
The devices embed peripherals allowing mathematical/arithmetic function acceleration (CORDIC for trigonometric functions and FMAC unit for filter functions).

They offer two fast 12-bit ADCs (4 Msps), four comparators, three operational amplifiers, four DAC channels (2 external and 2 internal), an internal voltage reference buffer, a low-power RTC, one general-purpose 32-bit timers, two 16-bit PWM timers dedicated to motor control, seven general-purpose 16-bit timers, and one 16-bit low-power timer.

– Three SPIs multiplexed with two half duplex I2Ss

The devices operate in the -40 to +85 °C (+105 °C junction) and -40 to +125 °C (+130 °C junction) temperature ranges from a 1.71 to 3.6 V power supply. A comprehensive set of power-saving modes allows the design of low-power applications.

All RF and IF tuning are accomplished automatically within the IC which eliminates manual tuning and reduces production costs. The result is a highly reliable yet low cost solution.

All IF filtering and post-detection (demodulator) data filtering is provided within the SYN470R, so no external filters are necessary. One of four demodulator filter bandwidths may be selected externally by the user.

The SYN470R offer two modes of operation; fixed-mode (FIX) and sweep-mode (SWP). In fixed mode the SYN470R functions as a conventional super-heterodyne receiver. In sweep mode the SYN470R sweeps a wider RF spectrum. Fixed-mode provides better selectivity and sensitivity performance and sweep mode enables the SYN470R to be used with low cost, imprecise transmitters.
